en: The Ritual Manual for the Sequential Method of Creating Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India by Imperial Decree.
The primary principal body is a great yellow color, seated in the full-lotus posture upon a great precious lotus pedestal.
Above,
its flower has thirty-two petals;
between each of these are various small leaves.
It is adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of great maṇi jewels.
On the crown of the Honored One’s principal face there are three tiers,
and the number of his various heads is five hundred.
On the left and right of the front face, two additional faces are fashioned;
the right is named Lotus Face,
and the left is named Vajra Face.
The right [face] has a blue-green appearance;
the left is of a deep blue-white color;
the front face represents the Buddha Family.
Because this Great Being possesses a great body,
he is fully endowed with the ocean-assemblies of the three families;
the eight great bodhisattvas serve as his retinue.
Before the Great Being was the goddess Kanyākṣī, holding lovely flowers;
she also held the seat for the boy and the assembly of monks reciting the sutra.
Her form had the appearance of a seven-year-old child.
The third layer consists of twenty-eight assemblies of beings,
each with its own original form.
The mantra is as follows:
First is Guhyakapāla-vajrapuruṣa,
crimson-red in color and possessing three eyes;
he holds a vajra in his right hand.
The left hand is in a fist placed at the waist.
He is Ucchuṣma-yaṅkuśī;
his left hand holds a single-pronged vajra.
The right hand is in a fist placed at the waist.
The eight classes of *ṛṣikas* are green;
their right hands hold the sword of wisdom.
The left hand forms the three-pronged mudrā.
Trimaheśvarada is black,
red, and crimson in color, possessing three eyes and an expression of wrathful anger.
He wears a three-pronged trident as a celestial crown and uses vajra-jewels as a necklace;
his left hand holds a ritual mace (vajra).
In his right hand he holds a precious platter,
which is red on the inside and black on the outside;
it is surrounded by four *kumbhīra* demons.
White in color with a reddish tint;
his left hand holds a precious bow,
and his right hand holds a precious arrow.
Fifth is Paśupatī,
white-red in color,
holding a noose in his left hand.
His right hand rests upon his hip;
he is Puṇyabhadra Cāmaracintāmaṇi,
and his left hand holds a vajra-wheel.
The right hand is in the fist mudrā;
he is red in color;
there are seven Saccamoharas.
The left hand holds a precious banner upon which a phoenix perches;
the right hand forms the mudrā of granting boons.
The eighth is Kūlaṃtaka-Pañjika,
holding a vajra-rattle in his left hand and making a vajra-fist with his right hand.
White-red in color;
the nine Piśāca kings hold swords in their left hands.
His right hand rests upon his hip;
he is Daśaśakti Vidyādhara,
holding a bow in his left hand.
In his right hands he holds a trident, a vajra, and an arrow;
his color is yellow-black.
Eleventh is Brahmā-sambhava.
The color is reddish-white;
the left hand holds a precious vase,
and the right hand holds a three-pronged vajra.
The second section is the Pure Abode (Śuddhāvāsa) King Yama;
his color is purple-white,
and his left hand holds the banner of Yama.
The right hand holds a female phallus.
Thirteen: the King of the Śākyas, thirty-three;
his color is white-red.
The left hand rests upon the waist;
the right hand holds a vajra.
This is the Sattva of the Fourteen Great Eloquence Qualities.
She is the daughter of Śakra Devendra, a goddess of great virtue,
and the chief consort of the god Vaiśravaṇa.
In her left hand, she holds a cintāmaṇi jewel.
He is purple-garnet in color.
His right hand holds a vajra-sword.
Fifteenth is King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
Her color is vermilion-red with a bluish-white tint.
Her left hand holds a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi-rāja*) that is yellowish-blue and octagonal;
her right hand holds a sword.
The sixteen powerful goddesses, the Mothers and their retinues,
whose complexions are like [gold];
and seventeenth, King Virūḍhaka.
The color is red;
the left hand holds a pestle,
and the right hand grasps a sword.
Eighteenth is King Virūpākṣa,
whose complexion is white;
he holds a mallet in his left hand.
The one on the right holds a golden noose and is blue in color;
the nineteenth is Vaiśravaṇa, King of the Heavenly Kings,
who is deep blue in color.
The left hand holds a precious stūpa;
the right hand holds a vajra.
There are twenty golden peacock kings.
The body is golden in color;
the left hand holds a precious banner,
upon which is a peacock of exquisite and subtle hue.
He spoke immeasurable wondrous words.
As for the assembly of twenty-one or twenty-eight great seers (*ṛṣi*),
these are the twenty-eight celestial deities (*deva*).
The deity Īśāna is the foremost;
his body is blackish-red and white in color,
and he holds a vajra in his left hand.
With his right hand, he holds a vermilion platter;
he is adorned with a necklace made of vajra-jewels and twenty-two *maṇibhadra* gems.
The color is white and red;
the left hand holds a jeweled banner topped with a wish-fulfilling gem.
His right hand is in the *varada-mudrā* (the gesture of granting boons).
Twenty-three: The Great General Vajrapāṇi, named Phalava.
His body is crimson-red in color.
The left hand holds a vajra;
the right hand rests on the hip.
There are twenty-four [nāgas], including Nanda and Upananda.
The color of his body is reddish above;
his left hand holds a red lasso,
and in his right hand he holds a sword, from the tip of each of which five blackish-blue dragons descend.
The left hand holds a blue rope;
the right hand holds a sword.
[This is] the Sāgara Dragon Īpala.
The complexion is reddish-white;
the left hand holds a red dragon,
and the right hand holds a sword.
The lower part of the body is blue-white;
in the left hand is a white dragon.
Twenty-fifth is Asura.
This refers to the asura Mahākāya.
His body is crimson-red in color;
his left hand holds a solar disc.
In his right hand is a moon disc;
he is a gandharva,
and in his left hand he holds a lute.
His right hand performs the dance mudrā;
his body is white and red in color.
He is the King of the Garuḍas.
Golden in color, she possesses two wings;
her left hand holds a conch,
and her right hand grasps a precious conch-flute.
The Kinnaras and Mahoragas—
these two kings have complexions as white as rākṣasīs;
they possess two eyes, or even three, four, or five eyes.
Holding various medicinal vessels and other implements,
she possesses two, four, six, or eight arms;
she is adorned with celestial crowns, divine garments, and various precious jewels as bodily ornaments.
Twenty-sixth, the deities of Water, Fire, Thunder, and Lightning.
These four deities are all complete with their spouses;
"Thunder" refers to the Thunder Deity of Heaven.
"Electricity" refers to the electricity of the earth.
These others take water and fire as their bodily ornaments.
There are twenty-seven Kumbhāṇḍa kings.
He has a long trunk and an expression of wrath;
he is black in color,
and his left hand brandishes a great vessel.
Holding a lasso in his right hand,
he is accompanied by twenty-eight piśācas;
Mahāmukha has a wrathful form.
Blackish-red in color,
his left hand holds a fire-jewel.
This is the first secret mantra of Guhyakapāla Vajra, the tenth secret utterance.
Oṃ agne agne svāhā. Oṃ uṣṇīṣa-mantra.
Oṃ viśvate rātrālokṣata svāhā. Oṃ maheśvara-da mantra.
Oṃ asammūrcchita-sadā svāhā. (4) This is the secret mantra of Kumbhīra.
Oṃ vaśiny-ārya-samanta svāhā. (5) This is the secret mantra of Varuṇa.
Oṃ uṣṇīṣasamaya-vijaya-vijaya svāhā. (6) This is the secret mantra of Pūrṇacakra.
Oṃ pūrṇa-sadā-karaṇa karaṇa āroṣaṇīye svāhā. (7) This is the secret mantra of Satyamaṇḍala.
Oṃ pe daṇḍe gati arakṣa svāhā. (8) This is the secret mantra of Kūlaṇḍaka.
Oṃ gnāye bhautaye rakṣa svāhā. (9) This is the secret mantra of Pibgala.
Oṃ mārakṣaye ajarakṣaye namo śriye svāhā. (10) This is the vidyā-mantra of Guṇasampannā.
Oṃ mahādevyai svāhā. (11) This is the mantra of Brahmā-saṃbhavā.
Oṃ vara vara yakṣeśvara yakṣeśvara svāhā. (12) This is the secret mantra of the Pure Abodes of the twelve divisions.
Oṃ vara vara hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. (13) This is the secret mantra of the thirty-three [deities] of Śakra, King of the Gods.
Oṃ maṇikā śākyavajra vaiḍūrye svāhā. (14) This is the secret mantra of Great Eloquence and Merit.
Oṃ mahā-kurukullataye svāhā. (15) This is the secret mantra of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
Oṃ kṣatriye svāhā sarvasattvaviśodhani svāhā. (The secret mantras of the sixteen Mother Goddesses.
Oṃ hiri hiri dākṣi tudakṣi svāhā. (The secret mantra of Virūḍhaka.)
Oṃ he ī hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. (18) This is the secret mantra of Virūpākṣa.
Oṃ madhu-ki-pu-kṣa-ti svāhā. (19) This is the secret mantra of Vaiśravaṇa.
Oṃ namo devanavajra-ḍāka-parameṣṭhine namo viśvambharāya svāhā. This is the twenty-syllable secret mantra of the Golden Peacock.
Oṃ jyotir-jvālā-kara-prabhāsa-raśmi-pramocana-hūṃ-lakāra-oṃ-jvālā-svāhā. (21) These are the secret mantras of the great ṛṣis of the twenty-eight sections. (28)
Oṃ namo buddhadharmasaṅghānantarāyabindhye svāhā. (22) This is the secret mantra of Maṇibhadra.
Oṃ dhārakara kṣamanta svāhā. (23) This is the secret mantra of the Great General Saṃjñeya.
Oṃ ārya-samaye svāhā. (24) This is the secret mantra of Nanda and Upananda.
Oṃ kumani-pauṅkha svāhā. (25) This is the secret mantra of the asuras and gandharvas.
Oṃ jña jña ku-malike svāhā (26). This is the secret mantra of Water, Fire, and Lightning.
Oṃ kurape yau svāhā (27). This is the secret mantra of the Kumbhāṇḍa King.
Oṃ jaye ajaye svāhā. (Twenty-eight syllables. This is the secret mantra of Vaiśravaṇa.
Oṃ jaye jaye lindhe lindhe svāhā. Thus the benevolent deities spoke with one voice.
Each made a vow to proclaim the secret mantras that reveal their names,
and they led their respective retinues,
surrounding and guarding them on all sides— left, right, front, and back.
Recite "Svāhā. If there are good men or good women who maintain this mantra,
they may recite the mantra of the benevolent deity.
"Endowed with great majestic power," and so forth.
This was transcribed by the Venerable Jōgen in the third year of the Enpō era.
In the first year of Tenmei, the year of Chou (1781), the Master Jinin transcribed this from a copy held at Eshin-in in Uji.
Having now obtained that original manuscript,
it has been collated once with the transmission copy held at Jishin-in on this mountain.
Revised in the eighth month of the Kōwa era. Recorded by Kaidō of Jūshōin, Hasedera, after completing the collation and correction.

On the fourteenth day of the fourth month of the Kiei year (1823). On the twenty-sixth day of the middle autumn of the Kansei third year (1801), the above was completed after being collated against a copy transmitted by the Ajari Shuyō of Myōkenji, Chiba.
Dragon liver.
